To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new tool called infoZILLA, which extracts structural elements from bug report descriptions with near perfect accuracy.

(1) bug reports can be parsed into structural elements with near perfect accuracy; and (2) bug reports can then be used to train machine learning models that predict software faults with higher accuracy than using the raw bug reports.

(i) we can automatically detect structural information from bug report descriptions with near perfect accuracy, (ii) we can use such information to facilitate research in the field of software engineering and (iii) our approach is generic and can be used for any type of software artifact that is described in natural language.
